children: As Baton Rouge gets ready for the Texas-LSU matchup, Bloom Energy is joining the community off the field to support two organizations making a difference for families across Louisiana.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261113756487/en/

On Friday, Bloom Energy visited Baton Rouge Fire Station 12 to recognize the work of the Baton Rouge Area Foundation and Civic Collaborative Foundation, two organizations helping strengthen communities and support Louisianans in times of need. As part of the event, Bloom Energy presented each organization with a $10,000 donation.

“Keeping communities safe depends on the people and organizations that strengthen them every day,” said Natalie Sunderland, Chief Marketing Officer at Bloom Energy. “For decades, the Baton Rouge Area Foundation and Civic Collaborative Foundation have stood alongside Louisiana families and helped communities rebuild and move forward. We’re proud to support their work and the lasting resilience they’re building across Baton Rouge and South Louisiana.”

“We’re so thankful for Bloom Energy’s generosity in Baton Rouge, and for the tireless dedication of first responders everywhere,” said Chris Meyer, president and CEO of the Baton Rouge Area Foundation and Civic Collaborative Foundation. “This grant will allow our community to better prepare for disasters before they happen and equip the brave men and women of the Baton Rouge Fire Department to respond more effectively.”

Among the largest community foundations in the country, the Baton Rouge Area Foundation seeks to improve the quality of life in greater Baton Rouge and across south Louisiana by supporting local nonprofits, engaging community leaders and partnering with others to create positive regional change.

Civic Collaborative Foundation, a Baton Rouge-based nonprofit that shares leadership and administrative support with the Baton Rouge Area Foundation, provides temporary relief to individuals and families facing financial hardship after natural and man-made disasters along the Gulf Coast and helps Louisiana communities prepare for and recover from disasters.
The donations reflect Bloom Energy’s commitment to supporting the communities it serves and partnering with local organizations that are helping build stronger, more resilient communities.

Bloom will also be on campus Saturday ahead of the Texas-LSU game as ESPN Radio’s College Football Campus Tour powered by Bloom Energy brings its live broadcast and interactive Fan Zone to Baton Rouge.
